correlates.name: Rhino-orbital-cerebral mucormycosis
correlates.presentation: 52-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes admitted in ketoacidosis (glucose 540 mg/dL, pH 7.10). Three days of nasal stuffiness, right sinus pain and headache, now swelling around the right eye, double vision and a black patch of dead tissue on the right palate. T 38.5 C, HR 118.
correlates.workup: Biopsy of the palate lesion: wide, thick-walled, ribbon-like hyphae without septa, branching at right angles and invading vessel walls, with surrounding necrosis. Culture is difficult and often fails.
correlates.management: Emergency surgical debridement plus IV amphotericin B, while correcting the ketoacidosis.

correlates.name: Q fever
correlates.presentation: 42-year-old sheep farmer who helped deliver lambs in the barn the week before. Two days of severe headache, chills, muscle aches and a dry cough. T 39.4 C, HR 96, RR 20, SpO2 95%; crackles at the right base; tender liver edge.
correlates.workup: Sputum Gram stain: inflammatory cells only, no organisms seen (the organism is intracellular and stains poorly). Chest film: patchy right lower zone infiltrate. ALT 140 U/L.
correlates.management: Doxycycline. Follow patients with valve disease or immune suppression: years later the infection can return as subacute endocarditis with negative blood cultures.

correlates.name: Inhalational anthrax
correlates.presentation: 44-year-old man who sorts and cleans imported raw goat wool. Two days of fever, malaise and muscle aches, then a rapid slide into breathlessness and chest pain. T 39.6 C, HR 128, BP 84/50, RR 32, SpO2 88%; dull bases; no skin lesions.
correlates.workup: Chest film: widened mediastinum with bilateral pleural effusions and little lung infiltrate. Blood culture: large gram-positive rods in chains with central spores; capsule made of poly-D-glutamate rather than sugar.
correlates.management: Ciprofloxacin immediately with ICU support; once severe breathing symptoms and shock begin, untreated mortality approaches 100%.

correlates.name: Pneumonic tularemia
correlates.presentation: 38-year-old hunter who skinned and cleaned several wild rabbits 4 days ago. High fever, chills, headache, malaise, dry cough and chest pain on breathing in. T 39.5 C, HR 104, RR 24, SpO2 92%; crackles over both lower lobes; no skin ulcer.
correlates.workup: Gram stain: tiny gram-negative coccobacilli, mostly inside macrophages. Agglutination test (antibody titer) positive; the lab avoids culturing it. Chest film: patchy bilateral infiltrates.
correlates.management: Streptomycin. Humans are dead-end hosts: ticks keep the organism in wild rabbits, so prevention is avoiding ticks and handling game with care.

correlates.name: Pneumonic plague
correlates.presentation: 29-year-old field biologist in rural New Mexico who traps prairie dogs; 3 days ago she nursed a coworker who had a swollen, tender groin node and later a cough. Sudden high fever, chills, weakness, bloody cough and breathlessness. T 40.1 C, HR 132, BP 82/48, RR 34, SpO2 85%.
correlates.workup: Sputum and blood: gram-negative bacilli whose stain gathers at both ends of each cell; culture grows the same rods. WBC 24,000/uL.
correlates.management: Streptomycin at once: the inhaled form nears 100% mortality untreated. Prevention is rodent and flea control.
